correctness.rationale: Proved n upper bound; marker construction achieves n at q>=3. A collision between two deletions with equal cyclic outputs induces a site permutation; a fixed site would induce an impossible equality of two different deletions of a rooted proper linear word, so compatible permutations have <=floor(n/2) cycles. Counting assignments on cycles and union bounding over pairs and rotations proves the exact exceptional bound. Chromatic polynomial of C_n yields the denominator and the exponential rate sqrt(q)/(q-1)<1. Direct exhaustive C++ verification matches all ternary words through n=12, quaternary through n=7, and marker construction through n=256. Finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The n maximal output ambiguity is information-theoretically sharp, with a real alphabet-size transition: existing binary maxima are strictly smaller for n>=4, while three colors attain n for all n. Beyond an explicit marker construction, a quantified exponential full-shadow law establishes that global rotational collisions are atypical among cyclically proper nonbinary sources, giving a motivated structural population result for unrooted circular deletion-channel output supports.
